name: Dan Sullivan
role: U.S. senator from Alaska (2015–present), former Alaska attorney general and natural resources commissioner
summary: Sullivan promotes Alaska resource development, military strength and stricter border enforcement, alongside targeted public investment and healthcare funding. He favours state authority in selected social policies, opposes most abortions, and supported federal marriage recognition with religious exemptions.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His 2025 presentation says he supported raising the top rate from 37 to 39.6 percent for incomes above $25 million, a limited increase.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He urged regulation of prescription-drug middlemen while campaigning to ease energy permitting. His position varies by sector.

cut-welfare.rationale: He defended a targeted safety net and Alaska health funding while requiring work and tighter benefit administration. This is selective reform, not wholesale rejection.

limit-guns.rationale: He opposed the 2022 gun-control bill and pledged to resist legislation infringing the right to bear arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: He promoted major military and Coast Guard expansion alongside greater support for law enforcement.

decide-locally.rationale: He explicitly supported state authority over marijuana regulation and abortion decisions, rather than uniform federal control.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: His later vote protected recognition of valid same-sex marriages; he stressed religious safeguards and acknowledged earlier opposition to Obergefell. Support is qualified.

abortion-legal.rationale: His documented policy opposed most abortions with specified exceptions; he later backed Dobbs and reiterated his anti-abortion commitment.

open-borders.rationale: He supported border-wall funding and stronger enforcement; the evidence addresses present border policy rather than a distant borderless ideal.

limit-growth.rationale: His energy plan insists on growth and employment while rejecting shutdowns of productive industries for climate policy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His plan accepts emissions reduction but rejects sweeping economic restructuring and mandates based on catastrophic projections. It favours technology and market-led measures.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His jointly authored energy plan calls for expanding the nuclear fleet, including advanced and small modular reactors.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He sought federal Energy Department financing for Alaska LNG and promoted military-based AI infrastructure.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He explicitly defended work requirements for able-bodied beneficiaries, with exemptions and Alaska flexibility.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His 2026 address championed new oil leases, increased production and the Alaska LNG pipeline.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He accepted the electorate’s removal of Trump and said voters should decide whether he could hold future office.

separated-powers.rationale: He explicitly identified separation of powers as a constitutional value central to his judicial-selection criteria.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He urged strengthening NATO, increasing allied commitments and maintaining effective military cooperation.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He explicitly championed protections for churches and religious universities adhering to traditional marriage.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He treated the constitutional right to bear arms as a binding limit on legislation.

non-intervention.rationale: He supported attacks on Iran and said the United States could shape regime change, while leaving Iran’s political outcome to its people.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: He celebrated increasing Alaska’s share of federal-land resource revenue to 70 percent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: After condemning January 6 violence, he insisted that peaceful Trump supporters retain their political voice and expression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He signed a letter opposing treatment of gender identity as sex under Title IX, particularly in schools and athletics. This concerns that legal context.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: His signed letter explicitly describes sex as biological, binary and grounded in immutable reproductive characteristics.

pollution-taxes.rationale: He promoted a ten-year methane-tax moratorium, opposing this particular pollution levy.

notes: Living-person answers use documented positions, never party-based inference. Latest clear evidence is preferred: marriage recognition is qualified, and his support for a limited top-income tax increase is retained. Marijuana federalism is not legalisation of all recreational drugs. Medicaid support and criticism of Obamacare do not establish a position on universal healthcare as such. Support for military force is not automatically support for intervention for humanitarian reasons. Opposition to sentence reductions does not by itself establish a general view of prison rehabilitation. His relatives’ ancestry and third-party praise do not establish an Indigenous land-authority position. Direct downloads of Senate pages and PDFs were attempted but returned access denials; full browser-accessible texts were reviewed. All 490 statements were checked against the research.
